I found one bug in the uncommitted changes.

**`docs/service.py:38` — missing ownership check (authorization bypass / IDOR)**

`rename` calls `self.repo.get(doc_id)` directly instead of `self._owned(user_id, doc_id)`. The `user_id` argument is never used. Any user can rename any other user's document just by knowing or guessing its id. The `read`, `update_body` and `delete` methods all go through `_owned`.

This also breaks the guarantee in the `_owned` docstring. Documents that belong to other users should raise `NotFound`, so the API never reveals which ids exist. With this code, the same call gives different results depending on whether the id exists and who owns it:
- A nonexistent id raises whatever `repo.get` raises.
- Someone else's document is renamed successfully.

Fix:
```python
document = self._owned(user_id, doc_id)
```

The title validation (strip, empty check, 200-character limit) looks fine. One ordering note: it runs before the ownership check, so a non-owner gets a `ValueError` for a bad title before they get `NotFound`. That leaks nothing about the document, but you could move the ownership check first to keep the error behavior consistent.
